content:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout 'realtime-serve/v2' showing increased 5xx rate and latency > 2s for p99. Automated canary policy triggered.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: realtime-serve/v2 -> traffic 20% started at 2635001233. CI checks green.

Alex: seeing the alert. p99 heatmap up across us-east-1. Can anyone confirm error class?

Irina: 5xx are mostly 502 gateway from proxy to backend. Error logs show "KV cache miss overflow" flooding logs.

Sam: copying logs: ```
[2026-03-15T11:07:12Z] ERROR proxy: upstream 10.2.4.11:5041 connection reset - kv cache alloc failed
[2026-03-15T11:07:13Z] ERROR runtime: token fetch timeout for request xxxxx
```

Maria: Prod customer PMs pinged. A few requests from enterprise accounts returning errors. We should estimate customer impact.

Alex: quick check: is this candidate model variant incompatible with cache settings? I saw a config change in canary: `kv_cache_size=64mb` -> `32mb` in the last rollout.

Sam: Rollout notes also changed runtime quantization flags. Might increase memory churn.

Irina: Given rising errors and paying customers affected, I'd vote for immediate kill-switch/rollback. Can someone flip the feature-flag?

Alex: Flag name is `feature:realtime-serve-v2-canary-traffic`. I can flip it but want oncall ack. @Sam are you ok with manual kill?

Sam: go for it. I'll prep rollback steps and smoke tests.

Alex: flipping flag now -> @deploy-bot please drain canary traffic after flag flip. :warning:

deploy-bot: ACTION: feature flag `feature:realtime-serve-v2-canary-traffic` set to OFF by Alex at 2635001242. Initiating traffic drain.

incident-bot: NOTIFICATION: Canary traffic reduced from 20% -> 0% over 30s. Canary instances marked for safe-shutdown.

Irina: confirm 5xx rate dropped to baseline?

Sam: p99 latency trending down. 1m error rate back to baseline. Good. But we need rollback in case some canary instances still have bad state. Alex, do you want full rollback or just keep v1 serving?

Alex: plan: manual rollback to stable tag `realtime-serve@stable-2026-03-14`. Steps: 1) ensure canary drained 2) lock traffic routing 3) trigger rollback job 4) run smoke test suite. I'll run the commands:```
# lock routing
svcctl routing lock realtime-serve --reason "emergency rollback"
# trigger rollback
deployctl rollback realtime-serve --to stable-2026-03-14 --why "canary errors" --wait
```

Sam: started rollback job at 2635001260. watch logs: `deployctl tail realtime-serve --since 1m`

deploy-bot: JOB: rollback job `rb-2635001260` started. Estimated time 2-4 minutes.

incident-bot: PAGING: oncall handoff needed for post-rollback verification. @Irina you are primary oncall.

Irina: I’m here. Will run verification checklist. Maria, can you confirm customer-facing comms in flight?

Maria: Drafting status message. I'll post to status.redwood.ai and notify affected accounts. ETA 5m.

Sam: rollback job reports success at 2635001278. Instances now reporting version `stable-2026-03-14`.

Alex: running smoke tests: ```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/realtime -d '{"input":"hello"}' | jq '.status'
# expected status: "ok"
```

Irina: smoke tests pass on canary-proxy and bg workers. p99 latency back < 600ms. No 502s in last 2m.

Maria: status page updated: "We detected errors for a small set of requests during a canary rollout. We have rolled back to the previous stable version and are continuing verification. No data loss. Contact support if you see issues." :white_check_mark:

Alex: leaving a runbook note in incident tracker: `INC-2635` with timeline and root cause hypothesis (kv_cache size change + quantization churn).

Sam: follow-up actions: 1) repro in staging with smaller kv_cache and quantization flags 2) add circuit-breaker to proxy to avoid connection resets 3) telemetry alert to watch kv cache alloc errors. I'll file tickets.

Irina: I’ll keep monitoring for 30m then hand back to normal ops. If anything flares, re-open this thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Rollback completed and verification passed. Incident severity downgraded. Incident owner: Alex. Next update scheduled in 30m.

Alex: thanks all. Great quick coordination. :team-heart:
